subject: english-literature
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the set 19th-century novels on the Edexcel GCSE English Literature specification?
questions.explain: Jane Eyre by Charlotte Bronte is one of the prescribed 19th-century novels; the others are 20th-century texts studied elsewhere.

questions.q: Who is the author of the set novel 'Great Expectations'?
questions.explain: Great Expectations was written by Charles Dickens, who also wrote the set text A Christmas Carol.

questions.q: Which author wrote the set novel 'The Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde'?
questions.explain: Robert Louis Stevenson wrote Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde, one of the specification's 19th-century novel choices.

questions.q: The poetry section of Paper 2 studies poetry written since which year?
questions.explain: The topic is 'Poetry since 1789', reflecting the anthology's range from the Romantic period onwards.

questions.q: How many poems does each collection in the Edexcel Poetry Anthology contain?
questions.explain: Each Edexcel anthology collection contains 15 poems, one of which students study in full.

questions.q: Which of the following is an actual collection in the Edexcel GCSE Poetry Anthology?
questions.explain: The Edexcel collections are Relationships, Conflict, Time and place and Belonging; the other options belong to a different exam board.

questions.q: Who wrote the poem 'The Charge of the Light Brigade'?
questions.explain: Alfred, Lord Tennyson wrote 'The Charge of the Light Brigade' about the Battle of Balaclava in the Crimean War.

questions.q: In the unseen poetry task, what are students required to do?
options: Compare an unseen poem with an anthology poem
Write an original poem of their own
questions.explain: The unseen task requires a comparison of two contemporary poems that students have not studied before.

questions.q: In Paper 2 Section A, what source material is provided to help students answer the 19th-century novel question?
options: A printed extract from the novel
A full copy of the whole novel
A published critic's essay on the novel
questions.explain: The novel question is extract-based: a printed passage is provided which students analyse and link to the wider text.

questions.q: Which assessment objective, covering spelling, punctuation and grammar, is assessed in the 19th-century novel response?
questions.explain: AO4 rewards accurate spelling, punctuation and grammar, and is assessed on the 19th-century novel question.

questions.q: Which assessment objective requires students to show understanding of the contexts in which texts were written?
questions.explain: AO3 assesses understanding of relationships between texts and their contexts, and is assessed on the anthology comparison.

questions.q: Which assessment objective focuses on analysing a writer's language, form and structure using relevant subject terminology?
questions.explain: AO2 rewards analysis of the writer's methods (language, form and structure) and the effects they create.

questions.q: What does AO1 mainly reward in a student's response?
options: A personal, informed response supported by textual references and quotations
questions.explain: AO1 assesses a critical, informed personal response backed by appropriate references to the text.

questions.q: In the anthology poetry question, students compare the named printed poem with what?
options: Another poem of their choice from the same collection
questions.explain: Students compare the given named poem with one other poem they select from the same anthology collection.

questions.q: Why are the poems in the unseen poetry task described as 'unseen'?
options: They are not from the anthology and have not been studied beforehand
They are printed in an invisible font
They must be memorised before the exam
They are drawn only from the 19th-century novel set texts
questions.explain: Unseen poems are printed on the exam paper and are texts students have not previously studied.

questions.q: Which assessment objective is NOT assessed in the unseen poetry task?
questions.explain: Unseen poetry assesses only AO1 and AO2; context (AO3) is not required because students do not know the poems' backgrounds.

questions.q: A student writes about how Dickens uses weather and a dark setting to reflect a character's fear. Which assessment objective is this addressing?
questions.explain: Analysing the effect of the writer's descriptive methods, such as setting and pathetic fallacy, addresses AO2.

questions.q: When comparing anthology poems, a student explains how Victorian attitudes to social class shaped a poem's message. Which assessment objective does this show?
questions.explain: Linking a poem to the social and historical context in which it was written demonstrates AO3.

questions.q: Faced with two unseen poems in the exam, which approach best matches the demands of the task?
options: Compare the writers' methods and their effects across both poems
Summarise the plot of only the first poem
Discuss the biography of each poet
questions.explain: The unseen task requires comparison of the two poems' language, form and structure (AO2) alongside a personal response (AO1).

questions.q: A student is unsure which second poem to compare with the named anthology poem. What is the correct choice?
options: A poem from the same collection they have studied
Any unseen poem from the exam paper
A Shakespeare play studied in Paper 1
questions.explain: The comparison must be with another poem from the same anthology collection the student has studied.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE English Literature (1ET0) specification; Paper 2: 19th-century Novel and Poetry since 1789
